tagline: From the devil's racetrack to the Neuse, by way of Bentonville.
intro: The byway sets out from US 701 at Four Oaks on Devils Racetrack Road, where by the old story travelers could hear the hoofbeats of a horse carrying the devil. No one has ever seen the horse or its rider. The road heads east past Civil War markers to Bentonville, then wanders some 84 miles of back roads in all across the Neuse River farmland, through Grantham and Dudley and down to the river at Seven Springs, to finish in Trenton, the Jones County seat.
The soil is the river's doing, laid down over thousands of years as the Neuse and its creeks flooded and changed course.

moments.title: Bentonville Battlefield
moments.text: In March 1865 Johnston's army made its one real attempt here to stop Sherman, and the Harper House, the only building left from the battle, served as a Union field hospital.

moments.title: Cliffs of the Neuse
moments.text: Just off the road, cliffs rise 90 feet from the Neuse, their colored layers of sand, clay and shell bared by erosion, with laurel and other mountain plants growing there.

moments.title: Seven Springs
moments.text: Seven mineral springs drew guests to a Victorian resort here from 1881 to 1944, and three hurricanes since 1999 have left a town of 55.
